newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was maintaining its stronger stance as Thursday's local dealings wound down, but offshore dollar demand around the 4.55 level was limiting any further push lower.
The rand was last at 4.5495/5425 against the dollar from 4.5600/5630 late Wednesday.
Dealers had expected more of the local unit but long positions, which were viewed as expensive in terms of carry costs, failed to take profits in volume.
The market's call for Friday was for dollars to trickle in from offshore longs leading to a pre-weekend drift lower.
"There will be profit taking and for some offshore guys at the lower levels they have taken profits today," said one dealer.
"It's just a matter of the realisation slowly filtering through the market that perhaps it was just a touch overdone on Wednesday," he added.
Cross rate action yielded mixed results against major currencies with the rand last at 0.3845/3850 marks from 0.3856/3859 marks on Wednesday and 24.8215/8599 yen from 24.7179/7451 before.

Against sterling the rand opened firmer but then retraced some of its early gains after the Bank of England hiked interest rates 25 basis points. It was last quoted at 7.6741/6837 from its previous level of 7.6835/6936.
Relative stability in rand and gold prices cheered bonds early but yields moved back above Wednesday's close as interest in gilts waned.
At 1440 GMT, the benchmark R150 bond was yielding 14.250 percent from Wednesday's late level of 14.235 percent, above its intraday best of 14.20 pct.
Dealers said the market was unfased by a 0.9 percent month-on-month increase and 8.4 percent yearly rise in producer inflation in May which matched market expectations.

In a Reuters interview in London, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said the rand was not a candidate for appreciation but at same time noted the central bank had no predetermined policy to allow it weaken.
He also said the latest relaxation of foreign exchange controls had led to just 25 million rand leaving the country over 10 days.
Stals was critical of a recent DRI/McGraw Hill report which ranked South Africa as the riskiest bet of the 10 largest emerging markets.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 15.10 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said Wednesday's money market shortage rose to 6.456 billion rand from Tuesday's total of 6.099 billion rand.
Foreigners were net sellers of 294.26 million rand's worth of bonds on Wednesday after buying 270.295 million rand's worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal bond exchange turnover totalled 10.6 billion rand.
